Each student needs an ordered record of their session notes, with
the most recent note easy to find.

Let's add an immutable SessionHistory that keeps notes newest first.
withNote(...) returns a new history and leaves the original
unchanged, so the model can prepare a change before saving it.

Notes are ordered by instant rather than by clock reading, so notes
recorded with different time-zone offsets still sort correctly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix list formatting in User and Developer Guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The note examples list in the User Guide has no blank line before it,
and the Logic component steps in the Developer Guide are numbered 1 to
5. The SE-EDU Markdown standard asks for a blank line before every list
and for 1. on every ordered-list item.

Let's add the blank line and number every Logic step 1.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log only the command word of user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager logs the full text of every command, and MainWindow logs
the full text of a command that fails. AddressBookParser also logs the
arguments at FINE and the full input of an unknown command at FINER.
Parent phone numbers and emails from add, and lesson notes from note,
therefore end up in the log file, which the coding policy forbids.

Let's log at most the command word, such as [USER COMMAND][note], in
all four places. A first word that is not a known command is logged
as "unknown", since a mistyped command may start with a student's
name or phone number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Logging guide: Explain how to log user commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers adding log statements have no guidance on which parts of
user input are safe to log.

Let's point them to AddressBookParser#getLoggableCommandWord and
explain why the full command text must not be logged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Testing policy: Add the Gradle test configuration
commitResults.messageBody:
The testing policy recommends test commands for Jest and pytest only,
and does not say what happens when RELATED_TEST_CMD is empty.

Let's add the Gradle configuration this project uses, and state that
source changes fall back to FULL_TEST_CMD.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document how to enable the Git hooks
commitResults.messageBody:
Git does not enable the hooks in .beryl/githooks when the repository
is cloned, and neither the DevOps guide nor the testing policy says
how to enable them. The testing policy also still says the pre-push
hook protects only main.

Let's explain how to enable the hooks in the DevOps guide, and update
the testing policy to describe the default-branch rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document private helpers in note parsing and rollback
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager#restore and NoteCommandParser#parseIndex are non-trivial
private methods without header comments, and parseIndex names its
caught exception "pe" while the rest of the session note code uses
"exception".

Let's add header comments to both methods and rename the variable to
match the coding standard's example.

The session note code relies on invariants that nothing checks:
histories are ordered newest first, an added note appears in its
student's history, and every persisted note is loaded back.

Let's state them as assertions so that a bug breaking any of them
fails fast in development and tests, instead of corrupting the
history silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplicated setup in model and logic tests
commitResults.messageBody:
ModelTest builds the same address book with ALEX and INDICES_NOTE in
two tests, and four LogicManagerTest save-failure tests repeat the
same model setup.

Let's extract the setup into helper methods so each test shows only
what differs.

Obsolete MVP planning documents and the standalone PR-review notes
remain in the repository, so agents load outdated context and cannot
discover the review guidance.

Let's remove the MVP specification files, move the review guidance
into a reviewing-prs Beryl skill registered in every tool shim, and
keep the commit-message conventions in one section of the coding
policy.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#130] Tighten up behavior of add function (#132)
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command reports vague messages, silently absorbs unknown
prefixes such as x/value into the level, and can leave an empty data
file behind when the first save fails.

Let's report each failure as the problem followed by the add usage,
reject unknown lower-case prefixes while still accepting subjects such
as "E Math/A Math", and create the data file only through the atomic
write so a failed first save leaves no file behind.

The repository has a Markdownlint configuration and the agent policies
tell developers to run it, but there is no package.json, so the command
cannot run, and the configured rules do not fully match the SE-EDU
Markdown standard.

Let's add markdownlint-cli2 as a locked local dev dependency, document
the setup step, scope every documented command to changed files with
--no-globs, and enforce ATX headings and 1. numbering for ordered
lists. Markdownlint stays out of CI and Git hooks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Number same-second session notes in added order
commitResults.messageBody:
Session notes are timestamped to whole seconds. When two notes for a
student share a timestamp, SessionHistory places the note added later
below the earlier one, so it is shown as older and gets the lower
note number. The UG promises that [1] is the oldest note, and
"delete note" can then remove a different note from the one intended.

Let's,
* treat a newly added note as the newest among notes with an equal
  timestamp
* restore saved histories in their saved order through a new
  SessionHistory#of, instead of re-adding each note with withNote
* add AddressBook#setSessionHistory so loading sets each history once

Re-adding saved notes one by one would treat each later-loaded note
as newer and reverse same-second notes on every reload. Building the
history from the saved list with a stable sort keeps their order,
while hand-edited files that are out of order still load sorted.

Tests that relied on the old tie order now expect the note added
later to be listed first.

The DG says notes with equal instants keep the order in which they
were added, and that loading re-adds each saved note through
AddressBook#addSessionNote. Neither is true once same-second notes
are numbered in added order.

Let's describe how SessionHistory orders same-second notes and how
loading restores a saved history, and update the matching design-tree
entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Skip saving when a command changes no data
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager saves the data file after every command other than
deletions, including commands that change nothing, such as view, help
and exit. When saving fails, those commands fail with the save error,
so the user cannot open a profile or the help window, or exit with
the exit command. If the data file failed to load and could not be
backed up, running help or view also overwrites it with an empty
roster.

The save error also names the temporary file used for the write
rather than the data file, which confuses the user.

Let's,
* skip saving when the address book is unchanged after a command
* name the data file in both save error messages

Comparing the address book with the copy already taken for rollback
covers every command, including future ones, without each command
having to declare whether it changes data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document skipping saves for unchanged data
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says every command on the persistence path is saved, and that
a failed save reports the storage exception's message. Neither is
true once commands that change no data skip saving and save errors
name the data file.

Let's describe both in the logic flow and the save-failure rollback
section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show a specific error for invalid note indices
commitResults.messageBody:
NoteCommandParser reports every index problem as an invalid command
format. For input in the right format whose index is wrong, such as
"note 0 nt/text" or "note x nt/text", the user is told the format is
wrong instead of what is wrong with the index.

Let's report that INDEX must be a positive integer when the text
before nt/ is a single word that is not a positive integer, and keep
the format error for an empty or multi-word preamble.

This matches how "delete note" reports its invalid indices, so both
note commands give the same kind of error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the invalid note index error
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says the note command reports an invalid index as an invalid
command format, and its manual testing steps expect that error for
"note 0 nt/text" and "note x nt/text". Neither is true once invalid
indices get their own message.

Let's describe the new error in the note command section and give it
its own manual testing step.

AddressBook#resetData replaced the persons with one setter call, then
reset the students and rebuilt the session histories inline. Mixing
these levels of abstraction made readers trace the loop to see that it
only copies each student's history.

Extract the student reset and the session-history copy into private
setters, so resetData reads as three steps at the same level. Behavior
is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#168] Update link to user guide in help window (#169)
commitResults.messageBody:
The Help window points to the course template's User Guide URL, so
users who copy the link land on a guide that is not TutorTrack's.

Let's point it to the team's own User Guide site, and update the UI
test and the Developer Guide's manual testing steps to expect the
new link.

MainApp.VERSION is still AB3's V0.5.1, so the startup log reports a
version that does not match any TutorTrack release.

Let's set it to V1.4 to match the upcoming release tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename AddressBook to TutorTrack in JAR and logs
commitResults.messageBody:
The JAR, the log file and the startup log messages still use the AB3
name AddressBook, which does not match the product users download.
The JAR also has to be renamed by hand for every release.

Let's name the JAR tutortrack.jar and the log file tutortrack.log,
say TutorTrack in the log messages, and update the JAR path in the
DevOps guide.

The data file stays at data/addressbook.json, so users of v1.3 keep
their roster after upgrading. Package and class names are unchanged
because users never see them, and renaming them now would conflict
with most open work.

commitResults.messageTitle: MainAppTest: Test startup and shutdown logging
commitResults.messageBody:
The log messages that MainApp writes on startup, on shutdown and when
the data file cannot be loaded are not tested, so a wrong app name or
version in them would go unnoticed.

Let's test that start() logs the version and starts the UI, that
stop() logs the shutdown and saves the user prefs, and that an
invalid data file logs the empty roster warning.

init() stays untested, because it reads and writes preferences.json
and the data file in the working directory, so a test of it would
depend on each developer's local files.

TutorTrack still saves its data in data/addressbook.json, an AB3 name
that users see when they open the data folder to back up or edit
their roster.

Let's save it in data/tutortrack.json, and update the Developer Guide
to match.

Users of v1.3 will start v1.4 with an empty roster, because the app
no longer reads the old file. Let's add a User Guide FAQ entry that
explains how to rename the old file to get their data back, rather
than adding migration code for a single earlier release.

commitResults.messageTitle: LogRecorder: Accept actions that throw checked exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
LogRecorder.captureMessages takes a Runnable, so a test that records
the logs of a method that throws a checked exception, such as
MainApp.init(), has to catch and rethrow it inside the lambda.

Let's accept an action that may throw, and rethrow its exception
after the recording stops. Existing callers compile unchanged, since
an action that throws nothing is inferred to throw only unchecked
exceptions.

commitResults.messageTitle: MainApp: Make file paths in init() testable
commitResults.messageBody:
MainApp.init() builds its storage from fixed paths in the working
directory, so a test cannot run it without reading and writing each
developer's own preferences.json and data file. The startup banner
and the data file path therefore have no tests, and the Codecov patch
check fails.

Let's read both paths through protected methods, so a test can point
init() at a temporary folder, and test init() and the default paths.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student add flow in UML (#178)
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide's diagrams still showed AddressBook-Level3's person
classes and had no view of how a student is added, so the guide did not
match TutorTrack's student model or UI.

Let's add a sequence diagram for the successful add path, update the
Model, Storage and UI class diagrams to show students, and explain the
add flow in the guide. Let's also record the course UML notation in a
policy file that the agent instructions point to, so later diagram
changes follow the same rules.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add activity diagram for save-failure rollback
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Save-failure rollback" section explains only in prose when
LogicManager saves a command's changes, skips saving, or restores the
data after a failed save. Readers have to trace these branches
through a long paragraph.

Let's add an activity diagram of this workflow next to that text.
It shows the copy, the unchanged-data check and the rollback branch,
with a note that deletion previews and confirmed deletions follow
their own path.

An activity diagram suits this better than a sequence diagram, as
the point is which branch runs rather than which objects interact.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add session note classes to Model diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The Model class diagram shows how AddressBook holds students, but not
where their session notes live. Readers of the Model section cannot
see that notes are kept beside the student list instead of inside
Student.

Let's add StudentSessionHistories, SessionHistory and SessionNote to
the diagram, and mention them in the Model section's bullets.

StudentSessionHistories keys each history by StudentId. The diagram
already shows StudentId as a part of Student, so a UML note states
the keying instead of a second association that would contradict
that composition.

Let's also remove the <<Rectangle>> stereotype from the Model package.
It renders as a «Rectangle» label, which is not course notation, and
the package is already drawn as a rectangle by the shared style.

The wider diagram is shown at a larger width so that its text stays
close to the size of the body text.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Explain new diagrams in surrounding text
commitResults.messageBody:
The save-failure rollback diagram follows a long paragraph that
already walks through every branch, so the diagram and the text
repeat each other. The session note model text also does not point
readers to the Model class diagram that now shows its classes.

Let's explain the rollback diagram one branch at a time after it,
in the same order as the diagram, and admit in a note what the
diagram leaves out: commands that fail and the deletion paths.
Let's also link the session note model section to the Model class
diagram.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#210] Sort names with numbers in numeric order (#220)
commitResults.messageBody:
The roster compares names character by character, so "Student 10"
is listed before "Student 2". Tutors who number their students or
siblings expect them in numeric order.

Let's compare runs of digits in names by their numeric value,
ignoring leading zeros, and compare other characters without regard
to case. The phone number and student ID remain tie-breakers, so the
order stays stable.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#214] Explain a missing note number in edit note (#223)
commitResults.messageBody:
When the note number is left out of edit note, the parser shows only
"Invalid command format!" and the usage, so the user has to compare
their input with the usage to find what is missing.

Let's detect when only a student index is given, and say that
NOTE_NUMBER is missing and that it is the number shown beside the
note in the profile.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#218] Refuse to save over a read-only data file (#219)
commitResults.messageBody:
TutorTrack writes to a temporary file and moves it over the data
file, so a read-only data file is silently replaced and loses its
read-only permission. The User Guide says the command should be
cancelled with an error instead.

Let's check that an existing data file is writable before writing,
and throw AccessDeniedException if it is not, so that LogicManager
shows the permission error and restores the previous data.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#211] Sort accented names with their base letters (#221)
commitResults.messageBody:
Names starting with an accented letter are sorted after every
unaccented name, so "Ålice Tan" appears below "Zoe Lim", where it is
easy to miss.

Let's strip diacritics before comparing names, and map letters that
do not decompose, such as Ø and Ł, to their base letters. The
natural numeric ordering still applies, and the original name stays
as a tie-breaker so the order is stable.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#213] Report oversized edit note numbers as too large (#224)
commitResults.messageBody:
edit note reports a student index or note number that is too large
to parse as not positive, which is wrong and confuses the user.

Let's tell the two cases apart, and say that the value is too large
when it exceeds the largest supported index.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report the specific rule a session note breaks
commitResults.messageBody:
note and edit note reject empty, overlong and non-printable text with
one generic message, so users cannot tell which rule they broke or by
how much a note is too long.

Let's check each rule in ParserUtil#parseNoteText, shared by both
parsers, and report the broken rule as a value error. An overlong
note's error states the length entered.

SessionNote keeps MESSAGE_CONSTRAINTS for the constructor and storage,
where no command format applies.

The User Guide and Developer Guide describe note-text errors as one
generic message.

Let's list the overlong-note message, note that empty and multi-line
notes have their own messages, and add a manual test for a
501-character note in note and edit note.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the single nt/ rule for session notes
commitResults.messageBody:
note and edit note reject a second nt/ after a space as a repeated
prefix, but the User Guide does not say so or explain how to mention
nt/ in a note.

Let's state the rule and the workaround of writing nt/ without a
space before it, record the decision in the Developer Guide and
design tree, and add parser tests for the workaround.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor UI and parser code for quality (#260)
commitResults.messageBody:
Several UI and parser classes mixed screen-geometry maths, nested
lookups and positional magic numbers into their main logic, which made
them hard to read and test.

Let's,
* move the screen-geometry maths from MainWindow into
  ScreenBoundsCalculator, and edit distance into EditDistance
* flatten the scroll lookups in SelectableText and StudentProfilePanel
* name the argument positions and counts in the note parsers
* add null checks, an assertion and a log line where they were missing

Behaviour, messages and FXML are unchanged.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/EditNoteCommandParser.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review of note-text error messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The guides did not quote the empty-note and non-printable messages,
and the Developer Guide's empty-note manual test still described the
old length rule. The check order for a note breaking several rules
was also undocumented.

Let's quote both messages, expect the empty-note message in the
manual test, and document and test that an overlong note with a tab
reports its length first.

SessionNoteTest held raw U+2028 and U+2029 characters, which editors
can silently change, so write them as escapes instead.

#246 set a standard for command errors, but a few messages were
missed and still read differently. One of them, `delete note 1 2 3`,
blamed a misplaced /confirm instead of the extra number.

Let's,
* report extra delete note values as "takes only one STUDENT_INDEX
  and one NOTE_NUMBER"
* report a /confirm anywhere but last as a misplaced /confirm
* word missing add values as "Missing sub/SUBJECT." and repeated
  prefixes as "n/ must appear at most once."
* say what to do next for two model-state errors
* report stray text in edit instead of treating it as a second index
* add Format and Example lines to the edit note typo hint

commitResults.messageTitle: Add HomeFolder to locate the JAR's folder
commitResults.messageBody:
TutorTrack resolves its data, preferences and log files against the
working directory, so launching the JAR from another folder reads and
writes files outside the folder containing the JAR. The course limits
the app to that folder and its subfolders.

Let's add HomeFolder, which finds the folder containing the running
JAR and resolves app files inside it. When TutorTrack is not running
from a JAR, as in development and tests, it falls back to the working
directory so those runs behave as before.

It also gives the display form of a path relative to the home folder,
so the status bar can keep showing a short path instead of an absolute
one that includes the OS user name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store data, preferences and logs in the home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
MainApp and LogsCenter name preferences.json, data/tutortrack.json and
tutortrack.log relative to the working directory. Launching the JAR
from another folder writes those files there and shows an empty roster
even when the folder containing the JAR holds the tutor's data.

Let's resolve all three files through HomeFolder so they stay with
the JAR wherever it is launched from.

FileHandler treats % in its pattern as a placeholder, and %t points to
the system temporary folder, so the log path is escaped to keep a home
folder such as "100%tutors" from sending the log elsewhere.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the data file relative to the home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
The status bar shows the data file by prefixing its path with "./".
Now that the data file path is absolute, it would show the full path,
such as /Users/<name>/.../data/tutortrack.json. That is long at small
window sizes and exposes the OS user name in screenshots.

Let's show the path relative to the home folder, as before, and fall
back to the full path only when the file is outside the home folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG for home-folder file locations
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says the data file is relative to the working directory, which
no longer matches TutorTrack now that it keeps its files in the folder
containing the JAR.

Let's describe the home folder in the data-file section and add a
manual test that launches the JAR from another folder, the case that
the alpha bug report found.

# Conflicts:
#	docs/DeveloperGuide.md
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/logic/parser/EditNoteCommandParserTest.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the v1.3 upgrade FAQ from the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The FAQ tells users who upgraded from v1.3 to delete
data/tutortrack.json if it exists. A user who added students after
upgrading loses them, because TutorTrack does not merge the two files.

The FAQ only helps someone moving a v1.3 data file to v1.4. Users of
the current release never have data/addressbook.json, so the entry
adds risk without helping them.

Let's remove it. The upgrade steps belong in the v1.4 release notes,
the release that renamed the data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the data file in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide says the home folder contains the data file but never
names it. The removed v1.3 upgrade FAQ was the only place that gave
data/tutortrack.json, so users can no longer find the file to back up,
move or edit.

Let's name the file in "Saving the data", say that TutorTrack creates
it on the first command that changes data, and tell users to copy it
while TutorTrack is closed to back up their roster.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#270] Fix crash on launch from a read-only folder (#271)
commitResults.messageBody:
Since logs moved into the home folder, launching from a write-protected
folder crashed before any window opened. FileHandler failed, and the
catch block warned through LogsCenter's static logger, which is still
null while the base logger is being set up.

Let's,
* warn through the base logger instead and carry on with console
  logging only
* tell users in the User Guide to pick a writable folder
* describe the fallback and add a manual test in the Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Update session note and data storage sections in UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide did not say how session notes are stored or what
happens when the data file is edited into an invalid state, so a
tester editing a note by hand could lose the roster without warning.
It also left out the note command's success message and how note
numbers are assigned.

Let's,
* add an "Editing the data file" section with the session-note fields,
  their rules, and a caution about invalid data files
* state the note command's timestamp, numbering and success message
* state that commands that do not change data still work while saving
  fails

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG for session note and data storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG has no manual test for a save that fails while TutorTrack is
running, so testers cannot check that a failed save leaves the data
unchanged and that commands which change nothing still work. Its
data-file section is also one long paragraph that is hard to scan,
and it uses "home folder" without defining it.

Let's
* add a "Saving fails while TutorTrack is running" manual test,
  using a read-only data file on Linux, macOS and Windows
* split the home-folder and data-file details into short lists
* define "Home folder" in the Glossary

The new test was run against the built JAR, and every message quoted
in the DG was checked against the code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap session-note lines over the soft limit
commitResults.messageBody:
Some Javadoc, constant and test lines in the session-note, home-folder
and logging code run past the coding standard's 110-character soft
limit, and one message constant breaks in the middle of its text.

Let's,
* re-wrap those lines at a higher syntactic level
* keep MESSAGE_EMPTY_NOTE's text on one line
* drop a doubled blank line at the end of LogsCenter

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the magic values in session-note code
commitResults.messageBody:
Session-note validation repeats the minimum length 1 as a literal in
the validity check, its error message and the parser, the JSON field
names are repeated as strings, and the user-command log line is built
from a string that its tests copy.

Named constants keep each value in one place, so the limit, the field
names and the log format cannot drift apart.

Let's,
* add SessionNote.MIN_TEXT_LENGTH and use it wherever 1 meant it
* name the recordedAt and text JSON fields once
* add LogicManager.USER_COMMAND_LOG_FORMAT and use it in its tests
* use Function.identity() for the note-count map keys

The messages and logged text are unchanged, which new and existing
tests check against the literal text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check session-note inputs at their boundaries
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON adapters and getLoggableCommandWord fail on null input only
deep inside, the timestamp parse failure is dropped when it is turned
into an IllegalValueException, AddressBook repeats the student search
that ReadOnlyAddressBook#getStudent already does, and HomeFolder's
null code-source check cannot be reached from a test.

Checking arguments where they enter makes the contracts explicit,
keeping the cause helps diagnose a bad data file, and reusing
getStudent removes the duplicate search.

Let's,
* reject null sources in the JSON adapters and getLoggableCommandWord
* keep the DateTimeParseException as the cause of the load error
* reuse getStudent in AddressBook#hasStudentWithId
* move the code-source check into a testable toCodeLocation helper

Tests for the session-note, logging and home-folder code cover the
common partitions but miss some boundaries and invalid-input cases:
placeholders FileHandler expands other than a bare %, the home folder
itself, empty and differently cased command words, the shortest and
longest valid notes, a note missing both fields, and the log line
written when a failed save is rolled back.

Let's add a test for each, named after the partition or boundary it
covers, and check that the rollback log leaves out the note text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share repeated commands in LogicManager tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage-failure and logging tests in LogicManagerTest spell out
the same note command and add command several times, so changing one
of them means finding every copy.

Let's name the note text, the note command and the add command once
as constants and use them in those tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix FAQ on moving data to another computer
commitResults.messageBody:
The FAQ told users to install TutorTrack on the other computer and
overwrite the data file it creates. TutorTrack needs no installer, and
it only creates the data file after the first data-changing command,
so there may be no file to overwrite.

Tell users to copy the JAR and their data folder instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check literal log lines in LogicManager tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Two LogicManager logging tests build their expected log line from
USER_COMMAND_LOG_FORMAT, so changing that constant would change the
production log line and the expected value together, and the tests
would still pass.

Asserting the literal text again makes each test check the log format
independently of the code under test. UNKNOWN_COMMAND_WORD returns to
package-private, since no test outside the parser package needs it.

Upstream master adds last-edited timestamps to session notes, which
conflicts with this branch's named constants and new tests in
SessionNote, JsonAdaptedSessionNote and their tests.

Let's,
* keep MIN_TEXT_LENGTH in MESSAGE_CONSTRAINTS alongside the new
  EDITED_AT_CONSTRAINTS
* keep the JSON field-name constants and name lastEditedAt the same
  way
* keep both sides' new tests
* expect recordedAt to be reported first when both fields are missing,
  since master now validates the timestamp before the text

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the parse cause for invalid lastEditedAt
commitResults.messageBody:
A malformed recordedAt keeps its DateTimeParseException as the cause
of the load error, but a malformed lastEditedAt drops it, so the two
timestamp checks give different diagnostic detail.

Let's keep the parse failure as the cause for lastEditedAt too, and
test it the same way as recordedAt.

commitResults.messageTitle: [#174] Keep four lines visible in the result display (#292)
commitResults.messageBody:
The result display could shrink to about 69 px at the default window
size, because the window's VBox shrinks each child toward its minimum
height when the children's preferred heights exceed the scene, and the
minimum was only 64 px. The last line of the delete previews, which
tells the user how to cancel, was cut off.

Let's,
* give the result display a minimum, preferred and maximum height of
  100 px, enough for four lines, so the roster and profile workspace
  absorbs the shrinkage instead
* add UI tests that check both delete previews and a four-line message
  fit at the default size and at 1280x720 with 150% scaling
* explain the height in the Developer Guide and add the "every line
  visible" check to the manual tests

commitResults.messageTitle: [#290] Report the real mistake in delete and edit errors (#294)
commitResults.messageBody:
Four mistakes in delete and edit got an error that described a
different mistake. delete 1 /CONFIRM counted the flag as a second
index, delete notes 1 1 was reported as extra indices, and
edit 1 em/foo was reported as stray text.

Let's,
* report /confirm in the wrong case as "must be typed in lowercase"
  in both delete forms, before the argument count is checked
* suggest delete note when the first word looks like a typo of note,
  sharing the typo check that edit note already uses
* report prefix-like stray text in edit as an unknown parameter
* update the User Guide error list and the Developer Guide tests
